title: Bread Flour vs All-Purpose Flour: The Difference Is Protein

seo.title: Bread Flour vs All-Purpose Flour
seo.meta_description: Bread flour commonly contains about 12–14% protein versus roughly 10–12% in U.S. all-purpose flour. The extra protein builds more gluten and changes chew, water absorption, and structure.
seo.search_intent: Compare bread flour and all-purpose flour by protein, gluten, and use.

excerpt: Bread flour commonly has about 12–14% protein compared with roughly 10–12% in U.S. all-purpose flour. That extra protein gives dough more gluten-forming potential, producing stronger, chewier bread.
content_html:
Bread flour and all-purpose flour are both wheat flour, but their protein levels give dough different strength. Bread flour commonly contains about 12–14% protein, versus roughly 10–12% for U.S. all-purpose flour.

Protein becomes gluten structure

When flour is hydrated and mixed, gluten-forming proteins build an elastic network. More protein gives that network more potential strength, which helps dough hold fermentation gases.

Bread feels chewier for a reason

Bread flour works well in bagels, pizza, and high-hydration loaves because it supports stretch and chew. In cakes or tender biscuits, that same strength can be a disadvantage if too much gluten develops.

Brand protein levels overlap

One all-purpose flour may be near 10% protein while another approaches 12%, so the category is not a single number. Comparing grams of protein per serving can help, though labels round values.

Substitution usually works with texture changes

All-purpose flour can make bread, but the loaf may be a little softer and absorb slightly less water. Bread flour can replace all-purpose in some recipes but may make the result chewier.

The useful rule

Choose bread flour when structure and chew matter; choose all-purpose when you want versatility and a more moderate gluten potential.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Bread flour, generally around 12–14% versus roughly 10–12% for all-purpose flour.

faq.question: Can all-purpose flour make bread?
faq.answer: Yes. The loaf may be a little softer and need slightly less water.

faq.question: Can bread flour replace all-purpose?
faq.answer: Often, but it can make cakes, cookies, or biscuits chewier.
